name: LA-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a PVI of R+20
Scalise is a well-funded, senior incumbent with $10.6M raised
Democratic challenger raised only $143K with minimal cash
Prediction markets price Republican win at 96%
model.rationale: Scalise holds a heavily Republican New Orleans-area seat with a massive financial advantage and no polling or ratings suggesting vulnerability, while markets give him a 96% chance of winning. The fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit Republican margin.
model.watch: A major national wave toward Democrats or an unexpected Scalise scandal could narrow the margin, though a flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Louisiana's 1st District is a solidly Republican seat covering suburban New Orleans and the Florida parishes, with a partisan lean of about 20 points toward the GOP. Steve Scalise, the House Majority Leader and a veteran incumbent, is seeking reelection with a large war chest of $3.9 million on hand from $10.6 million raised.

His Democratic opponent, Lauren Jewett, has raised only about $143,000 and has little cash available, with no outside spending or independent polling in the race. Prediction markets give Scalise roughly a 96% chance of winning. The forecast expects Scalise to win by a wide, roughly 19-point margin, consistent with the district's strong Republican lean and his incumbency advantage.
